why.title: Why this viewer exists
why.lead: An unofficial reader for a resource Google DeepMind released weeks ago, with an ancestry gap that no one has measured yet.
why.p1: In June 2025, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome API, a sequence-to-function model that predicts eleven molecular modalities from up to 1 Mb of DNA. The work was published in Nature on 28 January 2026. On 8 September 2026 came the AlphaGenome Atlas: precomputed predictions for roughly 9 billion single-nucleotide variants, summarized in a score called AVI (AlphaGenome Variant Impact) with per-feature SHAP attributions.
why.p2: The official library renders those results with matplotlib: static images, one per chart. This project shows the same results in the browser, interactively: the AVI contribution waterfall, the biosample-by-modality heatmap, a zoomable track browser, a position-by-position saturation map, and splicing and 3D-contact views. None of it calls the live API: the pipeline queries it once, with a personal key, and freezes the result into files; the web only reads them.
why.p3: The real reason to build it is a specific gap in how the AVI was trained. Its training label uses FAF95_GRPMAX: the lower confidence bound of the maximum filtering allele frequency across gnomAD's genetic ancestry groups (afr, amr, eas, mid, nfe, sas). The amr group is part of that maximum, and a variant that segregates on Indigenous American haplotypes but is diluted inside amr — which is an admixed group, not an Indigenous sample — can end up with a low aggregate FAF.
why.p4: None of the 18 features that feed the AVI includes frequency or ancestry: the model cannot learn to recognize that context directly. So the correct hypothesis is not that the AVI deliberately 'penalizes' Andean variants, but something more subtle: if a low FAF entered as noise in the training label ('proxy impactful' when FAF95_GRPMAX < 0.001), that noise could propagate as a systematic score inflation for variants with that frequency pattern. This is a calibration hypothesis, not an accusation against the model, and the version this project sets out to test uses gnomAD's local-ancestry VCF (7,612 samples, 14,804,206 SNPs), not the Peruvian sample from 1000 Genomes.
why.p5: That hypothesis has not been run yet: it is milestone H7 on the roadmap, and it remains pending. A null result — the AVI turning out to be well calibrated on that set too — would be published with the same weight as a positive one. This project's data contract does not even allow marking a study as conclusive without declaring sample size, statistical power, and limitations: that is an engineering rule, not a promise.
why.p6: Writing this from Lima does not change the science, but it does close an omission: the Atlas technical report explicitly asks for 'evaluating these tools across diverse genetic ancestries', and across the whole document the word 'ancestry' appears only twice. No sequence-to-function model has been evaluated on a population of predominantly Indigenous American ancestry. Any future work on that data would follow the CARE principles for Indigenous data governance: aggregate, open-consent data only, no claims about individuals or specific communities.
why.p7: What keeps this interface working a year from now rests on three constraints, not a promise: hosting is shared, with no persistent processes, so the build output is static files and nothing else; the API key is personal and non-transferable, so the web never uses it and only reads what the pipeline already froze; and the use is non-commercial and research-only, with the AlphaGenome Output Terms of Use shown on every page with derived content. None of the three depends on an external service staying online.
why.p8: Everything shown here is a model prediction, not an experimental measurement. It is not a medical device and should not be used for clinical decisions.
roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.lead: What is done, what is left, and the gates that decide whether the population study can run.
roadmap.noDates: No promised dates for what is planned: each item moves forward when its gate or its check allows it, not before.
roadmap.item.H0.name: Access verification
roadmap.item.H0.body: 39 probe calls against the API. The AVI's 18 features were resolved by name and family, and the contribution waterfall closes: base plus the sum of contributions reproduces the raw score.
roadmap.item.H1.name: Data contract and fixtures
roadmap.item.H1.body: Seven JSON Schema definitions, 86 test artifacts, and 51 tests that validate shape and byte budget before any real file reaches production.
roadmap.item.H2.name: Pipeline skeleton
roadmap.item.H2.body: A resumable acquisition layer — an interrupted run does not redo finished work — and a mandatory provenance stamp on every artifact: source, client version, date, and calibration epoch.
roadmap.item.H3.name: V1 and V2 views
roadmap.item.H3.body: The variant card (AVI contribution waterfall) and the biosample-by-modality heatmap, in both color themes and with no console errors.
roadmap.item.H4.name: Real data for three loci
roadmap.item.H4.body: First run against the real API, not synthetic, covering PPP1R1A/PDE1B, RASGEF1B, and RPL13A.
roadmap.item.H5.name: Track browser
roadmap.item.H5.body: Predicted REF versus ALT signal across the locus, with gene annotation below, wheel-driven zoom, and two resolution levels: an overview in 128 bp bins and 1 bp detail near the variant.
roadmap.item.H6.name: Deployment
roadmap.item.H6.body: Site live, served from a subfolder, verified with a real browser: zero console errors and zero requests outside its own host, which is how it is confirmed that the web never calls the API.
roadmap.item.N1.name: Saturation map
roadmap.item.N1.body: For a 512-position window, the AVI of all three possible alternative bases at each position. Sequence motifs stand out as contiguous columns of strong color.
roadmap.item.N2.name: Cross-linking between views
roadmap.item.N2.body: Every view of a variant links to the other available views of that same variant, without losing the locus context.
roadmap.item.N3.name: State in the URL
roadmap.item.N3.body: Locus, variant, view, visible tracks, and zoom level are all encoded in the URL: any state of the viewer can be shared as a link.
roadmap.item.V4.name: Splicing sashimi
roadmap.item.V4.body: REF versus ALT junction arcs for DNM1 in glutamatergic neurons, from a dedicated API call with its own ontology term, instead of reusing the locus's default biosamples.
roadmap.item.V5.name: Contact-map difference
roadmap.item.V5.body: A 3D contact diff for CELSR2/PSRC1 (rs12740374) in HepG2. The measured result is that the structure does not reorganize — a 1.46% change against the existing relief — and the view states it in numbers instead of auto-scaling the color.
roadmap.item.H7.name: Andean Atlas population study
roadmap.item.H7.body: Pending. It tests whether the same AVI score buys a different strength of evidence in variants enriched for Indigenous American ancestry than in matched European variants. A null result will be published with the same weight as a positive one.
roadmap.item.N4.name: Comparator
roadmap.item.N4.body: A view for placing two variants or two loci side by side. Not yet built.
roadmap.item.N6.name: Track search
roadmap.item.N6.body: Search over biosamples and modalities inside the track browser, to find a specific track without scrolling the full list. Not yet built.
roadmap.item.N7.name: Gene view
roadmap.item.N7.body: A panel centered on a whole gene instead of a single variant. Not yet built.
roadmap.gates.title: Population-study gates
roadmap.gates.lead: Six feasibility checks, in order: if one fails, the study stops there and is reported, rather than moving on to the next.
roadmap.gate.G1: gnomAD v3.1's local-ancestry VCF exists and is reachable without authentication or requester-pays charges, with its per-ancestry-component frequency fields confirmed in the header.
roadmap.gate.G2: A region can be extracted from the remote VCF without downloading the full file.
roadmap.gate.G3: gnomAD exposes FAF95_GRPMAX in a queryable way for the same variants, so per-ancestry-segment frequency can be cross-checked against the aggregate frequency.
roadmap.gate.G4: The Atlas API responds with the configured key, and the real response schema — including the 18 feature names — is documented against a test variant.
roadmap.gate.G5: Quota estimate: timing of a reference query at different concurrency levels, extrapolated to the study's real scale.
roadmap.gate.G6: A real, not estimated, count of how many variants meet the frequency criterion on a test chromosome, extrapolated genome-wide. If the total falls below roughly 2,000 variants, the study is published stating that it did not reach statistical power.
how.title: How it is built
how.lead: Three layers separated by a versioned data contract, with a byte budget and a provenance stamp checked on every build.
how.layers.title: Three layers, one boundary
how.layers.body: The Python pipeline runs locally, holds the API key, and is never deployed. Its output is frozen files under data/dist/. The web is static, with no backend and no frontend framework, and only reads those files: it does not know the pipeline's code and never makes a request outside its own host. The two layers communicate only through the data contract.
how.contract.title: Versioned data contract
how.contract.body: Every artifact follows a JSON Schema with a semantic version. A change that drops or retypes a field is major, and the web rejects it on screen instead of rendering something plausible but wrong. Studies are declared, not coded: a manifest names the panel types it wants, and the schema requires sample size, statistical power, limitations, and result direction before a study can be marked conclusive.
how.budget.title: Byte budget
how.budget.body: The budget is part of the contract, not a guideline: writing an artifact that exceeds it breaks the build. The initial index weighs 1,024 B against a 32 KB cap, time to interactive for every view is measured before and after each change on a simulated slow 3G connection (between 1.5 and 1.9 seconds, depending on the load of the measuring machine), and the track browser does 4.6 ms of work per frame against a 16.7 ms budget at 60 Hz.
how.provenance.title: Provenance stamp
how.provenance.body: Every artifact carries source, client version, query date in UTC, config hash, and calibration epoch, because the AVI's quantiles were recalibrated on 18 June 2026 and indel inference was fixed on 14 July 2026: comparing artifacts from different calibration epochs is invalid, and a score does not carry a label saying which one it came from. An artifact missing that stamp, or with a source outside the allowed set, breaks the build; synthetic data is marked as such and the interface shows it on screen.
how.tools.title: Data and tools
how.tools.lead: The exact versions of the data and client used to generate what is shown here, taken from each run's provenance stamp.
